newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Jaguar sees X200 pushing sales sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Jaguar sees X200 pushing sales sharply higher.

text.p: Jaguar expects its new smaller X200 model to spur sales to more than double last year's 40,000 cars, the automaker's Chairman Nick Scheele said Tuesday.

In an interview, Scheele said the luxury car maker, a unit of Ford Motor Co., would spend more than $800 million on the car, to be introduced in 1999. Two years ago, the company estimated it would spend $640 million on the vehicle, the smallest Jaguar ever produced.
Currently Jaguar produces the XJ6 saloon, and XK8 roadsters and coupes. The new model will compete with mid-priced German luxury cars such as BMW 5 series and the Mercedes E class.
Scheele said Jaguar would not reveal yet the range of engines that would be available for the X200.
"All I can say is that it will be class-leading, instantly desirable and incorporate the latest technology," Scheele said.

Jaguar will build the X200 at its new plant at Castle Bromwich in England. Ford persuaded Britain to present Jaguar with aid of $108 million to build the plant after it warned that it might build it in the United States.
Scheele said Jaguar had made great progress in recent years and was now profitable, although he declined to give details.
He would not rule out the possibility of building cars outside Britain. "BMW and Mercedes have shown that you can build outside your home base. Whether we will or not only time will tell," he said.
